definitions.explanation: Having the color of a clear sky.
Traditionally used for green things like traffic lights and unripe fruit.

examples.japanese: {青|あお}い{海|うみ}が{見|み}えます。
examples.english: I can see the blue sea.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}が{青|あお}くてきれいです。
examples.english: The sea is blue and beautiful.

examples.japanese: {目|め}が{青|あお}い{人|ひと}を{見|み}ました。
examples.english: I saw a person with blue eyes.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{空|そら}がとても{青|あお}くて、いい{天気|てんき}です。{外|そと}に{出|で}かけたいです。
examples.english: Today the sky is very blue and the weather is nice. I want to go out.

examples.japanese: {青|あお}い{信号|しんごう}で{渡|わた}る。
examples.english: Cross when the light is green.

examples.japanese: バナナがまだ{青|あお}いです。
{青|あお}い{葉|は}がきれいですね。
このりんごはまだ{青|あお}いので、{食|た}べられません。
examples.english: This apple is still green/unripe, so it can't be eaten.

examples.japanese: {信号|しんごう}が{青|あお}くなったら、{渡|わた}ってください。{日本|にほん}では{緑|みどり}の{信号|しんごう}を{青|あお}と{言|い}います。
examples.english: Please cross when the light turns green. In Japan, they call the green light 'blue'.

notes: Noun form: {青|あお}. Japanese traditionally used {青|あお}い for both blue and green. Modern Japanese has {緑|みどり} for green, but {青|あお}い is still used for traffic lights.
